violating.description: hello.txt is written without the trailing exclamation mark while count.txt still holds 19.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
greeting="Hello, graderproof!"
echo "${greeting%!}" > hello.txt
echo "${#greeting}" > count.txt

violating.description: count.txt is off by one because the newline is counted as a character.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
greeting="Hello, graderproof!"
echo "$greeting" > hello.txt
echo "$(( ${#greeting} + 1 ))" > count.txt

preserving.description: Uses printf instead of echo to write both files, with the same final content.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
greeting="Hello, graderproof!"
printf '%s\n' "$greeting" > hello.txt
printf '%d\n' "${#greeting}" > count.txt

preserving.description: Writes count.txt without a trailing newline.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
greeting="Hello, graderproof!"
echo "$greeting" > hello.txt
printf '%s' "${#greeting}" > count.txt

preserving.description: Computes the count with wc -m on the greeting text instead of shell length expansion.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
greeting="Hello, graderproof!"
echo "$greeting" > hello.txt
printf '%s' "$greeting" | wc -m | tr -d ' ' > count.txt

preserving.description: Writes count.txt first and hello.txt second, using a heredoc for the greeting.

files.solve.sh:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
greeting="Hello, graderproof!"
echo "${#greeting}" > count.txt
cat > hello.txt <<EOF
$greeting
EOF
